title: Signal-to-Customer: Tiered Comms and RCA Handoff for EU Capacity Regression
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-17 we observed a regression in the EU (eu-west-1) capacity pool that manifested as elevated 5xx rates and tail latency starting ~09:10 UTC after a kernel-level serving runtime rollout. This ticket coordinates customer-facing communications (status page cadence, follow-up notices, and targeted briefings) and formalizes the RCA handoff to the Platform Stability squad for actionable postmortem items and customer remediation offers.

Goals: (1) Provide a clear staged comms plan for customers of affected accounts, (2) Publish a concise statuspage timeline and follow-up update schedule, (3) Ensure the engineering RCA includes customer impact quantification and recommended SLA remediation (credits/waivers) where applicable, (4) Track ownership and ETA for each remediation action so PM/CS can brief paying customers.

Why this ticket: prior incidents (capacity/regression) had inconsistent customer follow-ups and delayed statuspage detail. This creates operational overhead for CS and erodes trust. We need a replicable template and a set of concrete postmortem actions with owners that drive closure within two sprints.

resolution_summary:
Immediate fix: rolled back the kernel rollout and applied a targeted scheduler parameter change to prevent scale-down suppression. Autoscaler hotfix merged (PR linked below). Short-term mitigation rebalanced the eu-west capacity pool and removed the tight affinity that caused pod placement delays. No data loss. Root cause (summary): a kernel scheduling tweak combined with an aggressive autoscaler scale-down policy caused transient pod startup latencies and KV cache cold starts at peak concurrency, which cascaded into increased 5xx responses for clients with pinned vhosts.

Customer impact quantification: ~18 customer accounts experienced >10% error-rate increases for 15-45 minutes; three enterprise customers with dedicated pools saw degraded throughput for up to 30 minutes. Estimated token impact: ~1.2M tokens reattempted. Proposed remediation: offer SLA credit for affected invoice window and targeted follow-up calls for top-affected accounts.
steps_taken: 09:26 UTC - Rolled back kernel rollout to prior stable release

10:30 UTC - Increased monitoring granularity and added synthetic traffic on canary routes to validate behavior
11:00 UTC - Confirmed error rates and latencies back to SLOs; continued observation for 48 hours
